chapters.title: Chapter 1151: Oka-san’s Soft Tits on My Chest
paragraphs: I groaned, my head falling forward slightly as I closed my eyes, my voice a low murmur. "You have no idea how hard that is right now, Oka-san..."

She giggled, the sound light and musical, and it was the most erotic thing I’d ever heard. The way her laughter wrapped around me, the way her breath hitched when I opened my eyes and locked onto her gaze—it was maddening. She knew she had me at her mercy, and she was loving every second of it.
Kasumi took a step back, her fingers finally brushing against my chest as she patted me lightly, as if she were trying to soothe a child.

But the contact only made the ache worse, the warmth of her hand seeping through my shirt, branding me. "There, there..." she said, her voice teasing, her eyes twinkling. "Just think of something else..."
I let out a sharp, disbelieving laugh. "Something else?" I repeated, my voice thick with amusement. "Like what, Oka-san? The weather?"

She nodded solemnly, though her lips twitched with a smile. "Yes. The weather. Or..." She tapped her finger against her chin, her voice dropping to a conspiratorial whisper. "You could think about Haruna..."

I groaned again, my head shaking as I let out a breathless chuckle. "You’re impossible..." I said, my voice a mix of exasperation and affection. "You know exactly that thinking about Haruna won’t help this situation..."

Kasumi’s giggles turned into full-blown laughter, the sound filling the space between us, warm and infectious. She pressed her hands to her mouth, her eyes shining with tears of mirth as she shook her head. "Jack..." she managed, her voice breathless. "You’re hopeless..."
I reached out, my fingers brushing against her wrist, pulling her hand away from her mouth. My touch was light, but it sent a shiver through her, her laughter dying down as her gaze locked onto mine.
The air between us was charged, thick with something unspoken but palpable—a tension that had been building since the moment she’d stepped out of that fitting room in nothing but lace.

For a moment, we just stood there, our breaths mingling, our eyes locked. The world around us faded away, the hum of the store, the soft music, the distant chatter of other customers—all of it melted into the background. There was only us, only this moment, only the heat of her skin against mine, the way her breath hitched when I traced my thumb over her knuckles.
Kasumi’s voice was a whisper, her eyes softening as she leaned into my touch. "Jack..." she said, her voice laced with something deeper, something more vulnerable. "You really need to calm down..."
I smiled, my voice a low murmur, the words vibrating between us like a shared secret. "I’ll try, Oka-san..."

My thumb continued tracing slow, deliberate circles on the inside of her wrist, her skin warm and soft beneath my touch. The contact was electric, sending sparks up my arm and straight to my chest. "But you’re not making it easy..."

Kasumi’s breath hitched, her gaze flickering up to meet mine. Her eyes were dark, a storm of shyness and desire swirling in their depths, and the way she bit her lower lip—her teeth pressing into the soft, pink flesh—made my pulse spike. It was a gesture so her, so full of longing and hesitation, that it sent a jolt of heat straight to my core.

For a moment, we just stood there, the air between us thick with something unspoken but palpable—a tension that had been building since the moment she’d stepped out of that fitting room, her body wrapped in nothing but lace and embarrassment.
The memory of it, the way she’d looked at me with those wide, flushed eyes, was enough to make my head spin all over again.
Then, with a soft, shaky breath, Kasumi’s voice came out barely above a whisper, her face still flushed a deep, rosy pink. "I am all yours..."
The words were simple, but they carried the weight of a promise, a vow. Her gaze locked onto mine, unflinching despite the shyness coloring her cheeks. "I am not going anywhere..."

Before I could respond, she did something that stole the breath from my lungs. Despite her shyness, despite the way her hands trembled slightly, she stepped forward and hugged me tightly, pressing her body against mine.

The warmth of her seeped into me, her soft, full breasts flattening against my chest, the fabric of her kimono doing little to dull the sensation. I could feel the rapid beat of her heart, the way her breath hitched as she melted into me.
"Does that feel better...?" she murmured, her voice muffled against my shoulder, her breath warm through the thin fabric of my shirt.

The contact was overwhelming. The scent of her—jasmine, warm skin, and that faint musk that was uniquely her—filled my senses, and I could feel the heat of her body through every inch of our pressed-together forms.

I didn’t answer with words. Instead, I leaned down, my lips finding the sensitive skin of her neck. She tasted like warmth and home, and I couldn’t resist the urge to press a kiss there, my lips lingering as I inhaled her scent.
The moment my mouth touched her skin, she let out a soft, breathy moan, her body trembling against mine. The sound was like music, a melody that resonated deep within me, and it only spurred me on.

My lips moved upward, trailing a path of kisses along the column of her throat, my breath hot against her skin. She tilted her head to the side, giving me better access, her fingers tightening their grip on my shirt as if she were afraid I’d disappear. The way she responded to me—so open, so trusting—made my heart ache.
"Jack..." she whispered, her voice a trembling breath, her body arching slightly into my touch. The way she said my name, like a prayer, like a plea, sent a shiver down my spine.
I pulled back just enough to look at her, my gaze drinking in the sight of her—her flushed face, her parted lips, the way her eyes were half-lidded with desire. My voice was rough, my throat tight.

"Oka-san..." I murmured, my hand cupping her cheek, my thumb brushing away a tear that had escaped her eye. I hadn’t even realized she was crying, but the glistening track on her cheek told me everything. "I am sorry... did I hurt you just now?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1152: Fumiko’s Whispered Caution
paragraphs: Kasumi’s breath hitched, her voice a whisper. "Jack..." She leaned into my touch, her hand covering mine, her fingers trembling. "No, you didn’t hurt me.. I am just happy... I love you "
The words hit me like a physical blow, and I felt my chest tighten. I leaned in, my forehead pressing against hers, my eyes closing as I let the moment wash over me.

The world around us faded away, the hum of the store, the soft music, the distant chatter of other customers—all of it melted into the background. There was only us, only this moment, only the heat of her skin against mine, the way her breath mingled with mine.

I kissed her then, my lips finding hers in a slow, deep press. It wasn’t hungry or desperate—it was tender, a kiss that carried the weight of everything we’d been through, everything we were, everything we could be.
Her lips were soft, warm, and they parted for me without hesitation, her breath mingling with mine as our kiss deepened.

When we finally pulled apart, Kasumi’s face was flushed a deep, rosy pink, her lips slightly swollen from the pressure of our kiss, her eyes shining with a mix of love, embarrassment, and something else—something that looked suspiciously like worry.

She rested her forehead against mine, her breath coming in short, panting gasps, her fingers still clutching at my shirt as if she were afraid to let go. "Jack..." she whispered, her voice trembling slightly, "we’re in public..."

I chuckled, my voice a low murmur, the sound vibrating against her lips. "I know, Oka-san..." I pressed one last, lingering kiss to her mouth, savoring the softness of her lips, the warmth of her breath. When I pulled back, my gaze locked onto hers, unwavering. "But I don’t care..."

Kasumi pulled back slightly, her chest heaving as she tried to catch her breath. Her eyes flickered downward, and I followed her gaze to the unmistakable bulge in my pants, still straining against the fabric. Her expression shifted instantly—her flush deepened, but not from embarrassment this time.
It was anxiety, pure and raw, that flickered across her face. Her fingers tightened around my shirt, her nails digging into the fabric as if she were trying to anchor herself.
I used my telepathy to tune into her thoughts, and what I heard made my chest tighten.

[What should I do...? Jack must be hurting a lot... He’s even injured... It’s not good for his health to do anything sexual... Because as his heartbeat increases, his blood flow will also increase... and he has an injury in his carotid artery... which might get hurt... But how should I say this to him...? Fumiko told me about this... secretly...]

The worry in her thoughts was palpable, a storm of concern and fear that she was trying so hard to hide. Her gaze darted back up to my face, her eyes wide and uncertain, as if she were searching for any sign of pain or discomfort.
The way she bit her lower lip, the way her fingers trembled against my chest—it was clear she was torn between her desire for me and her need to protect me.

I saw the worried expression settle over her face, her brows knitting together slightly, her voice catching in her throat as if she were trying to find the right words. But she didn’t say anything. She didn’t have to.

I took her hand in mine, my thumb brushing over her knuckles, my voice gentle but firm. "Oka-san..." I said, my gaze softening as I looked at her. "What happened?" I gave her hand a reassuring squeeze, my voice steady, my smile warm.

Kasumi’s eyes searched mine, her thoughts a whirlwind of doubt and relief.[Is he angry at me...?]The question echoed in her mind, her gaze flickering over my face as if she were trying to read my expression, to gauge my mood.
She must have seen something there—some reassurance, some sign that I wasn’t upset—because her shoulders relaxed slightly, though the worry didn’t completely fade from her eyes.

I could feel the tension in her, the way her body was still coiled with concern. She wasn’t just worried about my injury—she was worried about us, about the way we’d gotten carried away, about the fact that she’d been the one to pull back. But she didn’t need to apologize. Not for this.
Kasumi asked in a low voice, " Are you angry at me?"
I lifted her hand to my lips, pressing a soft kiss to her knuckles, my voice a whisper. "I’m not angry, Oka-san..." I said, my gaze never leaving hers. "I could never be angry at you..."

Kasumi’s breath hitched, her fingers tightening around mine as if she were afraid I’d let go. The relief in her eyes was evident, but so was the lingering guilt. She knew she’d been the one to stop us, and part of her was still wrestling with whether it had been the right decision.

I leaned in, my forehead pressing against hers once more, my voice a murmur. "You’re taking care of me..." I said, my thumb brushing away a fresh tear that had escaped her eye. "That’s all that matters..."

Kasumi let out a shaky breath, her voice barely a whisper. "Jack..." She leaned into me, her other hand pressing gently against my chest, right over my heart. She could feel its steady rhythm beneath her palm—a small comfort, proof that I was okay. "You promise you’re fine...?"
I noticed the bulge in my pants had calmed now. Seeing her emotional state, I didn’t press the matter.

I nodded, my voice soft but steady. "I promise, Oka-san..." I pressed another kiss to her forehead, my lips lingering against her skin. "Now, let’s go home... before Haruna starts thinking we actually forgot to buy her something..."

Kasumi let out a soft, watery laugh, the sound like music to my ears—light, fragile, and so her. She pulled back slightly, her fingers still tangled with mine, her gaze flickering between my eyes and my lips.

For a moment, it looked like she wanted to say something else—maybe to apologize for pulling away, maybe to confess how much she wanted to stay in that moment with me. But the words seemed to catch in her throat, her thoughts still tangled in worry and love.
Instead, she just nodded, her voice quiet, her grip tightening slightly as if she were afraid to let go. "Okay..."

We made our way to the counter, the black lingerie set already wrapped in sleek tissue paper. But as we stood there, I caught sight of the red set we’d talked about earlier—deep, passionate crimson, the lace even more daring than the black.

chapters.title: Chapter 1153: Kasumi’s Demand: Stay
paragraphs: Without a word, I pointed it out to the attendant, who nodded with a knowing smile and added it to our purchase. Kasumi’s face flushed anew, her free hand flying to her mouth as she let out a muffled, embarrassed sound.
The female attendant, ever the professional, pretended not to notice Kasumi’s flustered state, but I could see the amusement in her eyes as she rang up our items.

As we left the lingerie store, the weight of the bag in Kasumi’s hand seemed to amplify her embarrassment. She walked slightly ahead of me, her shoulders hunched as if she could hide from the world, her kimono swaying gently with each step.
I watched her, my heart full, the sight of her so alive—flustered, worried, but still mine—making everything else fade into the background.
Then, as if sensing my gaze, she glanced back at me, her eyes still wide with a mix of shyness and exasperation. "Jack..." she hissed, her voice a whisper, though there was no real anger in it.
I grinned, my voice warm. "What, Oka-san? You’re the one who looks like she’s about to faint..."
Kasumi groaned, her face burning as she turned away, but not before I caught the small, reluctant smile tugging at her lips.

We walked in comfortable silence for a moment, the city lights casting a golden glow over us. Then, I spotted a small boutique across the way, its window display filled with scarves in every color imaginable. I tugged Kasumi’s hand gently, guiding her toward it.
"Jack?" she asked, her voice curious but laced with exhaustion.
I didn’t answer right away. Instead, I led her inside, the chime of the bell above the door announcing our entrance.

The store was cozy, the air scented with lavender and something sweet, like vanilla. The walls were lined with shelves of folded scarves, their fabrics ranging from silk to wool, their colors vibrant and rich.
I browsed quickly, my eyes landing on a deep navy scarf—soft, lightweight, and just the right size to conceal the bandage on my neck.
I picked it up, running the fabric between my fingers to test its texture. Satisfied, I turned to Kasumi, who was watching me with a mix of confusion and concern.
I draped the scarf around my neck, adjusting it carefully so it covered the bandage completely.

The fabric was cool against my skin, a stark contrast to the warmth of Kasumi’s gaze as she took in what I’d done. Her eyes softened, a mix of relief and something deeper—gratitude, maybe, or the quiet acknowledgment of the lengths I’d go to protect them all.

"I don’t want to worry Haruna, Yuko, or Oba-san," I said, my voice soft but firm. The last thing I wanted was for them to see the bandage and spiral into panic. Not after everything we’d been through today. "Promise me, Oka-san... You won’t tell them about this either."

Kasumi’s expression softened further, her eyes glistening slightly as she reached out, her fingers brushing against the scarf. The touch was light, almost reverent, as if she were memorizing the feel of the fabric, the way it concealed the truth beneath. She nodded, her voice a whisper. "I promise..."

I let out a slow breath, my hand covering hers where it rested against the scarf. "After dropping you home," I continued, my voice gentle but resolute, "I will go out for a few days until my injuries are healed. Otherwise, living together, Haruna, Yuko, or Oba-san are bound to notice my injury..."
I gestured vaguely to my neck, the scarf shifting slightly with the movement. "As I can’t always cover my neck."

Kasumi’s face paled, her grip tightening on my hand as if she were afraid I’d disappear if she let go. "Go... go where?" Her voice was trembling, her eyes wide with a mix of fear and determination. "No... I... I will not allow it. You will stay with me."
I grabbed her hand, my thumb tracing circles over her knuckles, my voice soothing. "Don’t be nervous, Oka-san. It’s just for a few days, until I’m healed... and I will be back."
Kasumi shook her head, her voice firm but laced with panic. "What would you tell Haruna and the others?"
I considered for a moment, my gaze flickering to the shopping bags in her other hand. "Well, just tell them that I have some business to deal with..."
Kasumi’s breath hitched, her voice a whisper. "But..."
I reassured her with a squeeze of her hand, my voice warm. "It’s just a few days. I’ll be fine."

Kasumi’s worry didn’t fade, but she nodded, her fingers tightening around mine as we paid for the scarves and walked out of the shopping center. The night air was cool, the city lights casting a golden glow over us as we made our way to the car.
Kasumi drove, her grip on the wheel a little too tight, her knuckles white. I sat in the passenger seat, watching her from the corner of my eye, my heart aching at the tension in her shoulders.

She glanced at me, her voice agitated. "No... You arenotallowed to go. No matter what." Her voice was firm, her eyes burning with a mix of fear and determination. "I will think of something. Please... just promise me..."
I saw the worry etched into her face, the way her fingers trembled slightly on the wheel. She was terrified—terrified of losing me, even for a few days. And I couldn’t bear it.
I reached over, my hand covering hers on the gear shift, my voice soft. "Okay... Okay. I will listen to my wife." I gave her a small, reassuring smile. "I won’t go."
Kasumi let out a shaky breath, her shoulders sagging slightly in relief. Her voice was a whisper. "Thank you..."
We reached home and walked in together, me carrying the shopping bags, the weight of them a welcome distraction from the emotional weight of the day.

As we stepped inside, the warm glow of the living room lights enveloped us, the scent of dinner lingering in the air. It was almost 11:30 P.M., and the house was quiet, the only sounds the soft hum of the refrigerator and the distant murmur of the TV.

Yuko looked up from where she was sitting on the couch, her eyes lighting up as she took in the shopping bags. "You guys bought so much..." she said, her voice warm with curiosity as she took the bags from me, her fingers brushing against mine.
Tomiko, who had been sitting beside Yuko, turned to me, her expression concerned. "Jack... what did the doctor say?"
I kept my voice steady, my gaze flickering to Kasumi for a brief moment before answering. "It’s nothing. We met Doctor Fumiko..." I said, my tone light but firm. "She just asked Oka-san to rest."
Tomiko nodded, her shoulders relaxing slightly, though her eyes still held a flicker of concern. "That’s good..."

She walked slightly ahead of me, her shoulders hunched as if she could hide from the world, her kimono swaying gently with each step.
I watched her, my heart full, the sight of her so alive—flustered, worried, but still mine—making everything else fade into the background.
Then, as if sensing my gaze, she glanced back at me, her eyes still wide with a mix of shyness and exasperation.
"Jack..." she hissed, her voice a whisper, though there was no real anger in it.
I grinned, my voice warm.
"What, Oka-san?
You’re the one who looks like she’s about to faint..."
Kasumi groaned, her face burning as she turned away, but not before I caught the small, reluctant smile tugging at her lips.
We walked in comfortable silence for a moment, the city lights casting a golden glow over us.
Then, I spotted a small boutique across the way, its window display filled with scarves in every color imaginable.
I tugged Kasumi’s hand gently, guiding her toward it.
"Jack?" she asked, her voice curious but laced with exhaustion.
I didn’t answer right away.
Instead, I led her inside, the chime of the bell above the door announcing our entrance.
The store was cozy, the air scented with lavender and something sweet, like vanilla.
The walls were lined with shelves of folded scarves, their fabrics ranging from silk to wool, their colors vibrant and rich.
I browsed quickly, my eyes landing on a deep navy scarf—soft, lightweight, and just the right size to conceal the bandage on my neck.
I picked it up, running the fabric between my fingers to test its texture.
Satisfied, I turned to Kasumi, who was watching me with a mix of confusion and concern.
I draped the scarf around my neck, adjusting it carefully so it covered the bandage completely.
The fabric was cool against my skin, a stark contrast to the warmth of Kasumi’s gaze as she took in what I’d done.
Her eyes softened, a mix of relief and something deeper—gratitude, maybe, or the quiet acknowledgment of the lengths I’d go to protect them all.
"I don’t want to worry Haruna, Yuko, or Oba-san," I said, my voice soft but firm.
The last thing I wanted was for them to see the bandage and spiral into panic.
Not after everything we’d been through today.
"Promise me, Oka-san...
You won’t tell them about this either."
Kasumi’s expression softened further, her eyes glistening slightly as she reached out, her fingers brushing against the scarf.
The touch was light, almost reverent, as if she were memorizing the feel of the fabric, the way it concealed the truth beneath.
She nodded, her voice a whisper.
"I promise..."
I let out a slow breath, my hand covering hers where it rested against the scarf.
"After dropping you home," I continued, my voice gentle but resolute, "I will go out for a few days until my injuries are healed.
Otherwise, living together, Haruna, Yuko, or Oba-san are bound to notice my injury..."
I gestured vaguely to my neck, the scarf shifting slightly with the movement.
"As I can’t always cover my neck."
Kasumi’s face paled, her grip tightening on my hand as if she were afraid I’d disappear if she let go.
"Go... go where?" Her voice was trembling, her eyes wide with a mix of fear and determination.
I will not allow it.
You will stay with me."
I grabbed her hand, my thumb tracing circles over her knuckles, my voice soothing.
"Don’t be nervous, Oka-san.
It’s just for a few days, until I’m healed... and I will be back."
Kasumi shook her head, her voice firm but laced with panic.
"What would you tell Haruna and the others?"
I considered for a moment, my gaze flickering to the shopping bags in her other hand.
"Well, just tell them that I have some business to deal with..."
Kasumi’s breath hitched, her voice a whisper.
I reassured her with a squeeze of her hand, my voice warm.
"It’s just a few days.
I’ll be fine."
Kasumi’s worry didn’t fade, but she nodded, her fingers tightening around mine as we paid for the scarves and walked out of the shopping center.
The night air was cool, the city lights casting a golden glow over us as we made our way to the car.
Kasumi drove, her grip on the wheel a little too tight, her knuckles white.
I sat in the passenger seat, watching her from the corner of my eye, my heart aching at the tension in her shoulders.
She glanced at me, her voice agitated.
You arenotallowed to go.
No matter what." Her voice was firm, her eyes burning with a mix of fear and determination.
"I will think of something.
Please... just promise me..."
I saw the worry etched into her face, the way her fingers trembled slightly on the wheel.
She was terrified—terrified of losing me, even for a few days.
And I couldn’t bear it.
I reached over, my hand covering hers on the gear shift, my voice soft.
"Okay...
Okay.
I will listen to my wife." I gave her a small, reassuring smile.
"I won’t go."
Kasumi let out a shaky breath, her shoulders sagging slightly in relief.
Her voice was a whisper.
"Thank you..."
We reached home and walked in together, me carrying the shopping bags, the weight of them a welcome distraction from the emotional weight of the day.
As we stepped inside, the warm glow of the living room lights enveloped us, the scent of dinner lingering in the air.
It was almost 11:30 P.M., and the house was quiet, the only sounds the soft hum of the refrigerator and the distant murmur of the TV.
Yuko looked up from where she was sitting on the couch, her eyes lighting up as she took in the shopping bags.
"You guys bought so much..." she said, her voice warm with curiosity as she took the bags from me, her fingers brushing against mine.
Tomiko, who had been sitting beside Yuko, turned to me, her expression concerned.
"Jack... what did the doctor say?"
I kept my voice steady, my gaze flickering to Kasumi for a brief moment before answering.
"It’s nothing.
We met Doctor Fumiko..." I said, my tone light but firm.
"She just asked Oka-san to rest."
Tomiko nodded, her shoulders relaxing slightly, though her eyes still held a flicker of concern.
"That’s good..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1154: Tomiko’s Strange Behaviour
paragraphs: Haruna, who had been curled up on the other end of the couch, perked up at the sight of the shopping bags.

She quickly opened her gift, her face lighting up as she pulled out the dress Kasumi had picked for her. "Oka-san! It’s beautiful..." she exclaimed, her voice bright with excitement. She held the dress up against herself, twirling in front of the mirror to admire the fit.
Kasumi smiled, her voice warm. "I’m glad you like it, Haruna..."

Yuko and Tomiko opened their gifts next, their faces breaking into smiles as they took in the clothes Kasumi had chosen for them. Yuko held up her dress, her eyes sparkling. "This is perfect, Oka-san... Thank you..."
Tomiko nodded in agreement, her voice soft. "Yeah... Sister had a good choice..."
Haruna, never one to be left out, turned her attention to me. She noticed the scarf around my neck, and her eyes lit up with mischief.
"Jack, your scarf looks good..." she said, her voice teasing as she quickly closed the distance between us, throwing her arms around my neck in a playful hug.
Kasumi noticed that Haruna might hurt me as she hung on my neck, where I was just injured. She said with concern. "Haruna... what are you doing?"
She rushed forward, her hands gripping Haruna’s shoulders to pull her away. "Jack just took me to the hospital... How can you blame it on Jack? It is my fault..."

Haruna froze, her arms still wrapped around my neck, her face falling as she realized her mistake. She quickly let go of me, her hands flying to her mouth as she turned to Kasumi, her voice soft and guilty.
"Oka-san, this is not it... I was just playing around..." She stepped closer to Kasumi, her arms wrapping around her mother in a tight hug.
"I am just happy... that Jack can take care of you..." Her voice was muffled against Kasumi’s kimono, her words sincere. "I was just teasing him... It’s not your fault..."
Kasumi’s expression softened, her hands stroking Haruna’s hair as she held her close. "I know, Haruna..." she murmured, her voice warm. "But you have to be careful... Jack must be tired."
Haruna nodded against her mother, her voice a whisper. "I’m sorry, Jack..."
I ruffled her hair gently, my voice light. "It’s okay, Haruna... I know you didn’t mean it..."
Yuko and Tomiko exchanged a glance, their expressions a mix of relief and amusement. Tomiko’s voice was warm as she stood, stretching slightly. "Well, it’s late... We should all get some rest..."
Yuko nodded, her voice gentle. "Yeah... It’s been a long day..."
Kasumi let go of Haruna, her gaze flickering to me, her voice quiet. "Jack..." she said, her eyes still holding a flicker of worry. "You should rest too..."
I nodded, my voice soft. "I will, Oka-san..."

As the others started to disperse, heading to their rooms for the night, Kasumi lingered beside me, her hand finding mine once more. Her fingers were warm, her grip almost desperate, as if she were afraid I’d slip away if she let go. Her voice was a whisper, her gaze searching mine with a mix of worry and love. "Youpromiseyou won’t go anywhere...?"

I squeezed her hand, my thumb tracing circles over her knuckles, my voice a vow. "I promise, Oka-san... I’m not going anywhere..." The words settled between us, heavy with meaning, with the unspoken understanding that I washers—now and always.

Tomiko, ever the caretaker, clapped her hands together, her voice warm and practical. "Let’s have dinner. We were all waiting for you guys..." She gestured toward the dining table, where the maids had already begun serving the meal. The scent of steamed rice, miso soup, and grilled fish filled the air, the warmth of the food a comforting contrast to the emotional weight of the day.

We all gathered around the table, the chatter light and easy as we ate. Haruna regaled us with stories of her day, her voice bright and animated, while Yuko and Tomiko listened with amused smiles. Kasumi, though quieter than usual, seemed to relax slightly as the meal progressed, her worry easing with each bite, each laugh shared between us.

After dinner, Tomiko turned to Kasumi, her voice gentle but firm. "Sister, in order to get full sleep, you should sleep on the bed..." She placed a hand on Kasumi’s shoulder, her touch reassuring. "You’ve had a long day..."
Yuko and Haruna nodded in agreement, their voices soft but insistent. "Yeah, Oka-san..." Yuko said, her eyes warm with concern. "A good, sound sleep will be good for you..."
Haruna chimed in, her voice laced with a mix of affection and mischief. "And we’ll all sleep in our rooms too..."

I caught the flicker of reluctance in Kasumi’s eyes as she glanced at me, a silent question hanging between us. Do I have to? But she didn’t protest. Instead, she nodded, her voice quiet. "Okay..." She stood, her kimono swaying gently as she followed Tomiko toward her room.

Tomiko helped Kasumi settle into bed, tucking the blankets around her with a mother’s care. When she returned to the living room, she found Haruna and Yuko still lingering, their expressions a mix of curiosity and concern.

Tomiko turned to Haruna, her voice gentle but knowing. "Haruna, I think we should let Jack sleep alone tonight..." She hesitated slightly, her gaze flickering to me before continuing. "I’m afraid he won’t get good sleep... especially..."

Haruna’s face flushed a deep crimson, her eyes widening as the memory hit her—that night, when she’d been caught by Tomiko, her lips wrapped around my cock, her eyes wide with shock and embarrassment.

The memory was enough to make her nod quickly, her voice a whisper. "Y-Yes... Oba-san..." She ducked her head, her fingers twisting together as she practically fled to her room, her footsteps quick and light.
Yuko, sensing the tension, gave me a small, knowing smile before following Haruna, her voice warm. "Goodnight, Jack..."

Tomiko waited until the others had disappeared down the hallway before turning to me. She held out a steaming cup of tea, the aroma of chamomile and honey filling the air between us. "Drink this," she said, her voice soft but firm. "It will help you relax and remove your tiredness..."
I took the cup from Tomiko’s hands, the warmth seeping into my palms like a comforting embrace. The steam curled up, brushing against my face, carrying the soothing scent of chamomile and honey.
"Thank you, Oba-san..." I said, my voice sincere. The gesture was small but meaningful—a silent acknowledgment of the day’s events, of the worry we’d all carried, of the love that bound us together.

But as I lifted the cup to my lips, I noticed something strange in Tomiko’s expression. Her usual warmth was there, but beneath it, there was something else—a flicker of emotions that didn’t quite align.

A hint of relaxation, yes, but also excitement, and beneath that, a tension that made the air between us feel charged. Her eyes were bright, almost too bright, and her fingers tapped lightly against her thigh, as if she were holding back words or actions.
I took a sip of the tea, the liquid warm and slightly sweet, the flavor spreading through me like a gentle wave. But my gaze never left Tomiko’s face.
There was something there, something she wasn’t saying, and it made me pause, the cup halfway to my lips.

chapters.title: Chapter 1155: Tomiko’s Mysterious Tea
paragraphs: I used my telepathy to probe Tomiko’s thoughts, and what I uncovered sent a jolt of adrenaline through me, sharp and electric.
[I don’t know how long Jack is gonna stay... I can’t miss this opportunity... Now it’s great, he’s already taken a sip...]

Her thoughts were a whirlwind of urgency and something darker—desire, maybe, or desperation. My stomach twisted.Opportunity?What did she mean by that? And then, like a blade twisting in my gut, her next thought hit me with brutal clarity:

[The mixture should work fast... A blend of aphrodisiac and a mild sleeping agent... Just enough to lower his inhibitions, to make him... pliant... But not so much that he’ll be out cold. I want him to feel... I want him to want...]

My breath caught in my throat.Aphrodisiac?A sleeping drug? The warmth spreading through my veins wasn’t just from the chamomile—it washerdoing. My body already felt heavier, my thoughts slightly foggy, but my healing factor had kicked in the moment the first drop of that tainted tea touched my lips.

I could feel it working, neutralizing the foreign substances, burning through them like fire through dry grass. The drug was already being purged from my system, my body restoring itself to its natural state.
I had to play this carefully.

Tomiko turned back to me, her expression a perfect mask of concern, but her eyes—oh, her eyes—betrayed her. There was a flicker of something there, something hungry, somethinganticipatory. Her fingers tapped lightly against her thigh, a nervous habit, as if she were holding back words or actions. The air between us felt charged, thick with unspoken tension.
"Jack?" she asked, her voice soft, her hand still resting on my arm. Her touch was warm, almost too warm, and I could feel the slight tremor in her fingers. "Are you okay?"

I forced my voice to slur slightly, my words deliberate but slow, as if I were fighting to stay coherent. My mind raced, calculating.Aphrodisiac and a sleeping agent... So she wants me to be aroused but compliant?The idea was both unsettling and...intriguing.But I couldn’t let her know I was onto her. Not yet.

"Oba-san..." I said, my gaze locking onto hers, my voice thick. I let my head loll slightly, my vision blurring as if the drug were taking hold. But internally, I was sharp, my mind working overtime.What’s her next move?Would she try to undress me? Touch me? Or was this just a test, a way to see how far she could push?
Tomiko’s breath hitched, her fingers tightening slightly on my arm, her nails pressing into my skin through the fabric of my shirt.
For a moment, her mask slipped—just for a second—and I saw it: the flicker of guilt in her eyes, raw and unfiltered.

But beneath it, something else burned brighter:excitement.A thrill, dark and intoxicating, at the risk she was taking, at the taboo nature of what she was doing. It was a look I’d never seen on her before, and it sent a chill down my spine.

But then, just as quickly, the mask was back in place. Her expression softened into one of calm, almostmaternalconcern, her voice gentle but firm. "Let me help you to your bed..." she said, her tone laced with a warmth that felt almost too practiced.
I nodded slowly, my voice a murmur, my words deliberately slurred. "Mmm..." I let my body sway slightly, my steps unsteady as she guided me forward.
But my mind was razor-sharp, my senses heightened to an almost painful degree. Every touch, every breath, every subtle shift in her demeanor was magnified, analyzed.
And then I noticed it—she wasn’t leading me to the guest room.
We were moving deeper into the house, toward the hallway where the family’s bedrooms were located. My pulse spiked.Her room.She was taking me toherroom.
The realization sent a jolt through me. This wasn’t just about making sure I rested. This wasintentional.She wanted me inherspace, underhercontrol.
I let my body lean into hers, playing the part of the drugged, exhausted man. But internally, I was calculating, my mind racing.
The warmth of her body against mine was undeniable—her curves pressing into my side, the heat of her skin seeping through the thin fabric of her kimono.

The scent of her perfume—cherry blossoms with an undercurrent of something muskier, darker—filled my nose, and I had to fight to keep my expression neutral, to not react to the way my bodynaturallyresponded to her proximity.
As we reached the bed—herbed—I let myself sink onto the mattress, the sheets cool and smooth against my skin.

The room was imbued with her presence: the faint scent of her perfume lingering in the air, the soft, plush pillows arranged just so, the way the moonlight filtered through the curtains, casting a silver glow over the space. It was intimate.Toointimate.

Tomiko’s hands were everywhere as she helped me settle—guidingme,steadyingme, her touch lingering in places that weren’t strictly necessary. Her fingers brushed against my waist, my back, the side of my neck as she adjusted the scarf, her breath warm against my skin.
Was she testing me?Seeing how far she could push before I reacted? Or was she simply savoring the moment, the thrill of having me here, in her domain, under her influence?
I forced my eyes to flutter closed, my breathing to slow, my body to go limp, as if the drug were finally taking full effect.

But my mind was wide awake, my healing factor already working overtime to purge the last traces of the aphrodisiac and sleeping agent from my system. The effects were fading fast, but I had tosellit. Had to make her believe.

Tomiko tucked the blankets around me, her movements efficient butcareful—too careful. Her fingers brushed against my shoulder, her touch lingering, and I could feel the heat of her body as she leaned over me.

The scent of her was intoxicating, and for a moment, Ialmostforgot this was all an act. Almost let myself get lost in the warmth of her, the way her breath hitched when she thought I wasn’t paying attention.

"Sleep well, Jack..." she murmured, her voice a whisper, her breath warm against my ear. There was a pause, a hesitation, as if she wanted to say more but wasn’t sure she should. Then, her hand brushed against my cheek, her touch feather-light, almostreverent.
And then, her thoughts slipped through, unbidden, raw, andhungry.
[You have no idea how long I’ve wanted this... To have you like this... Helpless... Mine...]
My pulse spiked. This was therealher—the one beneath the mask of the caring sister, the doting aunt.

The one who had been watching, waiting, wanting. The realization was a punch to the gut. She didn’t just want me asleep. She wanted me to be aware. Aware enough to feel, to respond, but not enough to resist.
And then, the unthinkable happened.

Her other hand—the one I couldn’t see, hidden beneath the blanket—traced the line of my thigh, just for a second. Just a brush of her fingertips against the fabric of my pants, but it was enough to make my breath catch, my muscles tense. She was testing the waters. Seeing how I’d react. Seeing if I was truly under the influence.

I want to wear my clothes.

She had no idea how deeply the Lust Demon ability had already bound her to me.

I made my way toward Kasumi’s room, guided by the faint sound of muffled crying.
The door was slightly ajar.
I pushed it open quietly and stepped inside.
There she was, sitting on the edge of her bed, curled into herself with her face buried between her knees.
Her shoulders shook with each sob, the sound raw and heartbreaking.
Without a word, I crossed the room and wrapped my arms around her tightly, pulling her trembling form against my chest.
Kasumi stiffened for a brief second, then melted into the embrace, her face pressing into my shoulder as fresh tears soaked into my shirt.

I’m here," I murmured tenderly against her ear, my breath warm on her skin.

My gaze was steady and reassuring.
"Kasumi...
I will handle everything.
You don’t have to worry anymore."

chapters.title: Chapter 1184: Kasumi’s Shy Surrender
paragraphs: Kasumi’s heart visibly shattered. The confusion and shock on her face were painful to watch. Her beloved daughters were hitting and scolding the man she had just bared her soul to. Tears flooded her eyes as maternal panic and heartbreak took over.

"Stop it! Stop hurting him right now!" Kasumi lunged forward desperately, pushing Haruna and Yuko away with both hands. She dropped to her knees in front of me, cupping my face with trembling fingers.
"Jack... are you okay? Did they hurt you? Tell me truthfully—does anywhere hurt? I’m so sorry... I’m so sorry this is happening because of me!"
"I’m fine, really," I said gently, wiping her tears.
But Kasumi was far from calm. She turned to her daughters, shielding me with her body. "Why are you two doing this?! Don’t touch him! It’s not Jack’s fault at all! I’m the one who seduced him."

"I’m the guilty one here! Jack is completely innocent—blame me instead!" Her voice cracked with emotion. "Your mother is the indecent one... I should be the one being punished, not him. Please... just leave him alone."
Yuko tilted her head. "Oka-san, you’re really protecting him this much?"
Haruna added softly, "You look like you’re about to cry even more..."

Kasumi kept her arms spread protectively. "Of course I’m protecting him! He’s done nothing wrong. I was the one who started everything. If anyone has to be scolded, it’s me. Don’t hurt Jack anymore... I can’t bear seeing it."
Yuko and Haruna exchanged quick glances and finally dropped their fake anger. They rushed in and hugged their mother tightly from both sides.
"Oka-san, we don’t blame you at all," Haruna said warmly, rubbing her back. "We were just teasing."
"Yeah, it’s obviously all Jack’s fault," Yuko added with a playful grin. "He’s the big bad wolf here."
Kasumi still refused to move from her protective position in front of me. "No more hitting him... promise me."
Haruna stood up and crossed her arms, smiling. "Oka-san... do you love Jack? Be honest with us."

Kasumi’s face turned bright crimson. She looked anxious and nervous, like she was standing on a stage about to be judged. "I... I..." After a long, painful pause, she nodded shyly. "Yes... I do love him. I’ve loved him for a long time."
Yuko grinned. "Hmph, it took you so long to admit it, Jack. I was really starting to worry about you two."
Haruna chuckled. "He even got Aunt Tomiko yesterday, you know."
Kasumi blinked in utter disbelief. "Wait... what? What are you two even talking about? Tomiko too? How... how long has this been going on?"
Yuko pulled her mother into another tight hug. "Oka-san, I’m so happy right now. From now on, we’ll all be together forever... like real sisters."
"Sisters...?" Kasumi repeated, stunned. "You mean... all of us? With Jack? I don’t understand... Aren’t you angry? Aren’t you disappointed in me?"

Haruna shook her head gently. "Oka-san, you’ve sacrificed your own happiness for us for so many years. You always put us first. Now it’s your turn to be happy. Live for yourself. With Jack, everything will be fine—we promise."

I stood up and wrapped my arms around all three of them, pulling them into a big, warm embrace. "Oka-san, Yuko, Haruna... I love each and every one of you," I said sincerely. I kissed them one by one—first Haruna on the lips, then Yuko, and finally Kasumi on her forehead and then her lips.
Kasumi remained frozen in shock, her mind clearly overwhelmed. Haruna laughed softly at her mother’s dazed expression. "Look at Oka-san’s face! She’s so cute when she’s confused."
"You... you girls already knew about this...?" Kasumi whispered, still trying to process everything.
Yuko smiled brightly and nodded. "Oka-san, actually... it was mostly my idea. I wanted all of us to be together forever. No more secrets, no more loneliness."

Yuko then began explaining everything in detail—my special abilities, the power that had bound us together, the promise of immortality, and the beautiful, eternal future we could all share as one family. Kasumi’s eyes widened with every word, a whirlwind of emotions flashing across her face: shock, disbelief, wonder, and a flicker of hope.
She suddenly reached out with trembling fingers and checked my neck, carefully searching for any sign of injury or bandage.

When she found nothing, her expression shifted instantly from concern to realization. She slapped my chest lightly, though there was no real anger behind it—only flustered affection. "You... you were playing me this whole time!"
I chuckled softly and pulled her close again, wrapping my arms around her in a tight, protective embrace.

I could feel her heart racing against mine. "No, my love... if that situation had really happened, I wouldn’t hesitate to make that choice again. I would give anything for you—for all of you. You are worth every sacrifice."
Kasumi buried her face deeper into my chest, her body shaking with soft sobs. Her voice came out muffled and vulnerable. "Will you really love me...? Even though I’m older?"
I tilted her chin up gently so our eyes could meet. Brushing a tear from her cheek with my thumb, I spoke with all the warmth I could muster. "Kasumi... I don’t just love you. You are my heart."

"Every beat is yours. I love the way you sacrifice everything for your family, the quiet strength you carry, and the beautiful woman who has been hiding her feelings for far too long. You are not ’too old.’ You are timeless to me. I want to wake up every morning with you in my arms, to protect you, to cherish you, and to make you feel desired every single day."

Kasumi’s lips quivered, fresh tears spilling down her cheeks, but this time they were mixed with a shy, radiant smile. "Jack... I’ve been so scared. I thought I would lose everything... but hearing you say that makes me feel like I’ve finally come home."
Haruna sighed dreamily from the side, clasping her hands together. "So romantic... I’m getting jealous just watching you two."
Yuko grinned and leaned against my shoulder. "See, Oka-san? This is what we all wanted. Jack has enough love for every one of us. He’s going to spoil us rotten for eternity."
I kept one arm securely around Kasumi and reached out to pull Haruna and Yuko closer, forming a warm, intimate circle. "All of you are my world," I said softly, looking at each of them in turn.

"Haruna, your fire and playfulness light up my life. Yuko, your clever heart and strength bring me endless joy. And Kasumi... you are the gentle soul I want to grow old with—except we won’t grow old. We’ll have forever."

I leaned in and kissed Kasumi again, this time slower and deeper, pouring my affection into it. When we parted, I whispered against her lips, "You are mine, and I am yours. No more hiding. No more tears of doubt. Only love from now on."

Kasumi nodded, her voice barely a whisper but full of emotion. "I love you, Jack... I love you so much it scares me. But I don’t want to run away anymore. I want to stay by your side... with all of us together."
Haruna and Yuko exchanged happy glances before joining in, each stealing a quick kiss on my cheek while showering their mother with affectionate hugs.
The room felt lighter, warmer—filled with the promise of a shared future no one could break apart.

chapters.title: Chapter 1185: Julie’s Emergency Call
paragraphs: Kasumi gently pushed me away with both hands, her face flushed a deep, adorable shade of pink. She looked up at me with a shy, hesitant expression, biting her lower lip as if struggling to find the right words.

"Go take care of Tomiko first..." she murmured softly, her voice tinged with concern and a hint of lingering embarrassment. After a small pause, she added, "Tell me the truth, Jack... did you know the effect of the tea... and drank it anyway, knowing what would happen?"

I looked at her tenderly, taking her hands in mine and giving them a reassuring squeeze. I didn’t want any more secrets between us. "Well... to tell you the truth," I said calmly, "it was Oba-san who gave me the tea deliberately. She wanted to seduce me that night."

"When we went inside the room, I realized what was happening... but I just didn’t want her to feel awkward or ashamed. That’s why I pretended not to remember everything. I wanted her to feel safe and loved, not guilty."

Kasumi’s eyes widened in genuine surprise. She covered her mouth with one hand, staring at me in disbelief. "Tomiko... she really did that...?" Her voice was a mix of shock, understanding, and a touch of reluctant admiration. "All this time I thought she was just caught up in the moment, but she actually... planned it?"
I nodded, pulling her back into my arms despite her earlier gentle push. I rested my chin lightly on top of her head, holding her close.

"Yes. She’s been carrying a lot of hidden feelings for a long time. Just like you," I said softly, caressing Kasumi’s cheek. "But that doesn’t change how I feel about either of you. If anything, it makes me love her more—because it shows how deeply she wanted me, even if she was scared to admit it. And it makes me loveyoumore for caring so much about her happiness."

Before I could say anything else, Kasumi’s face turned an even deeper shade of red. With a shy but determined push, she placed both hands on my chest and gently shoved me toward the door. "Go take care of Tomiko first," she whispered, avoiding my eyes.

Behind her, Haruna and Yuko were mercilessly teasing their mother, giggling as they poked her sides and made exaggerated kissing sounds. "Look at Oka-san, all red and shy~" Haruna laughed. "She’s so cute when she’s in love!"
"Stop it, you two!" Kasumi protested, covering her burning cheeks with her hands, which only made her daughters laugh harder.
I smiled to myself as I left the room and walked down the hallway. I stopped in front of Tomiko’s door and knocked softly. "Can I come in?"
"Come in..." came Tomiko’s gentle voice from inside.

I opened the door and stepped in. My breath caught at the sight before me. Tomiko was wearing a beautiful purple yukata that hugged her figure elegantly, the soft fabric accentuating her curves. The color complemented her skin perfectly. I couldn’t help but stare, openly ogling her with clear admiration.
Tomiko noticed my gaze immediately. A bright blush bloomed across her cheeks. "Jack..." she said softly, her voice a mix of nervousness and quiet pleasure.

I didn’t waste another second. I closed the distance between us in two strides, wrapped my arms around her waist, and pulled her into a passionate kiss. I captured her lips deeply, pouring all my desire and affection into them.

Tomiko melted against me, her hands clutching my shoulders as I kissed her until she was breathless. When I finally pulled back, she was panting heavily, her chest rising and falling, lips slightly swollen and glistening.
Suddenly, my phone rang. I glanced at the screen—it was Julie. I answered quickly. "Hello?"
Julie’s worried voice came through urgently. "Jack... we’re taking Freya to the hospital right now. She’s about to give birth. If you can make it..."
"I’ll be there," I replied without hesitation.
I looked at Tomiko, guilt flashing across my face. "Oba-san... I’m so sorry. I—"

Tomiko smiled warmly, though I could see a hint of reluctance in her eyes. She reached up and gently cupped my cheek. "Go do your job. Knowing you, I know it must be something important. Don’t worry about me."
I nodded gratefully and pulled her into one last tight hug. "Thank you, Oba-san. I’ll come back as soon as I can. I promise."

Tomiko was clearly reluctant to let go, her fingers lingering on my arms for a few extra seconds, but she eventually released me with a soft, understanding smile. I gave her one final kiss on the forehead before walking out.
I quickly gathered Haruna, Yuko, and Kasumi and told them the news. "Freya is about to give birth. I need to head to the hospital right away."
All three of them immediately spoke up.
"We also want to go!" Haruna said excitedly.
Yuko nodded eagerly. "Yeah, we want to be there too."
Kasumi stepped forward, a shy but determined look on her face. "I... I also want to meet those other women."

I smiled warmly at their enthusiasm but shook my head gently. "I’ll bring all of you later. Right now, I should go ahead alone. I don’t want to overwhelm Freya, and I need to be there as fast as possible."
The moment I was out of sight, I focused my power and instantly teleported to Beverly Hills. I appeared directly inside the luxurious private hospital room Julie had sent a picture of.

Freya lay on the bed in a thin hospital gown that had slipped slightly off one shoulder, revealing the smooth, flushed skin of her collarbone and the generous swell of her full, heavy breasts. Her massive pregnant belly rose prominently, round and taut, glistening with a light sheen of sweat that made her look incredibly erotic.
Her long hair was messy, strands clinging to her neck and chest, and her face was flushed a deep, aroused pink from the contractions.
Even in labor, she looked devastatingly sexy—her thick thighs slightly parted under the sheet, her full lips parted as she panted, and her eyes heavy with a mix of pain and raw desire.
